newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee up on low import demand for dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee up on low import demand for dlrs.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee was firmer against the dollar in early Monday trade, mainly due to a lack of commercial demand for the greenback, dealers said.
At 0435 GMT the rupee was at 58.48 to the dollar, after opening at 58.55, they said.

"Demand for dollars is low mainly because there are no imports," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer. "Overseas easing of the dollar and the Central Bank's action are also contributing to a firm rupee."
Dealers said the Central Bank pushed down the dollar by 1.25 local cents in line with its overseas easing. Buying and selling prices were fixed at 58.3382 and 59.5168.
"The dollar-rupee exchange rate should remain around 58.45 and 58.65 during the week in the absence of imports and plenty of borrowers for call money," said a Hongkong and Shanghai Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates were at 11.5 percent after rising to 12 early, dealers said.
